name: Aaron
overview: Aaron was a male member of the tribe of Levi, known primarily as the brother of Moses and as Israel's first Levitical priest. His role was foundational in establishing the priesthood among the Israelites. No additional personal notes are recorded beyond these significant identifiers.
namesAndTitles: Aaron is the only recorded name for this individual, and no specific meaning or divine origin of the name is provided in the Scriptures referenced. The name is simply presented as his proper name.
familyAndRelationships: Aaron was the son of Amram and Jochebed, and the brother of Moses and Miriam. He was married to Elisheba and fathered Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar. Additionally, he is an ancestor to notable priestly figures such as Hilkiah and Seraiah. These relationships place him firmly within the Levitical lineage and priestly heritage.
scriptureSignificance: Aaron is significant in the biblical narrative as the first high priest of Israel, serving as a mediator between God and His people. He acted as Moses’ spokesman before Pharaoh and performed miraculous signs, demonstrating God's power. Despite his important role, he also experienced failure, as seen in the incident of the golden calf and his challenge to Moses’ authority. His priestly line continued through his descendants, foreshadowing the perfect high priesthood of Christ, who fulfills the ultimate mediatorial role.

keyEvents.event: Called by God to join Moses
